messages:
Sasha: morning — quick thread to coordinate shadowing/on-call onboarding for next week. I'm the new shadow and want to make sure we have clear primary/secondary handoffs + coverage gaps documented.
Maria: hey! welcome. i'll be primary Mon–Wed, Kevin Thu–Sun. you're shadowing me Mon–Tue.
Kevin: confirmed. i'll be secondary Mon–Wed and primary Thu–Sun. happy to take point for the weekend handoff walkthrough on wed afternoon.
Sasha: awesome. couple quick Qs: 1) where's the concise checklist i should run through during a live incident? 2) who covers paging if both primary & secondary are OOO?
Maria: checklist is here -> https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/Oncall+Quick+Checklist (short version at top).
Maria: TL;DR: confirm alert details, check runbook, triage severity, notify customer-impact channel, escalate to on-call lead if P1, open incident ticket.
Sasha: got it. any commands i should memorise?
Maria: basics: 
```
# check running model pools
redwoodctl pools status --env prod
# tail recent runtime logs
redwoodctl logs service/runtime --since 15m
```
Maria: also bookmark the KV cache health dashboard and the token-cost regression board.
oncall-bot: :bell: Pager triggered: INC-2041 by monitor/runtime-latency, severity: P2. Assigned to Maria as primary. (this is a system test page).
Sanjay: fyi — we run a simulated page drill today at 16:00 PT. Sasha, stay online for the drill, we'll walk through notifications and the escalation steps.
Sasha: perfect, i'll be there. for escalation: if primary doesn't ack in 5m, pager auto-routes to secondary, and 15m -> oncall-lead. correct?
Maria: yep. policy: 5m ack -> 10m initial mitigation -> 15m escalate to lead. all in the runbook.
Kevin: coverage gap note — Thu morning I have a calendar conflict 08:00–11:00 PT. Olivia offered to be backup for that window, Olivia can you confirm?
Olivia: yes i can cover 08:00–11:00 Thu. i'll be listed as emergency backup in rotation for that window.
Sasha: great — i'll add Olivia to my shadow checklist and ping her for the handover snippet.
Sasha: what's the recommended way to practice live mitigation during shadowing?
Maria: start with simulated incidents (we'll do one today). then watch a real P3 or P2 triage — you'll do the runbook steps with me talking you through. avoid taking primary action on P1 until cleared.
Sasha: makes sense. any notes about customer comms?
Maria: short and frequent updates in #customer-impact for any incident affecting latency or correctness. use this template: 
"Status: investigating — impact: X customers affected — ETA next update: 20m"
Kevin: also: if it's model-quality related, loop in the ML channel and tag @research for eval support.
Sasha: handoff logistics: what's the standard message to leave in the thread when handing over?
Maria: we do a short handoff in this format: 
"Handoff: primary -> primary (time window). current state: summary; actions taken: list; next steps: list; blockers: list; contact: who to call"
Sasha: can i get a sample handoff from last week to use as template?
Maria: i'll paste one after the drill.
Maria: sample: 
"Handoff: Maria -> Kevin 2025-11-12T18:00Z. current state: Elevated token latency on eu-west cluster. actions: scaled pool + rolled back quantization; next steps: monitor KV hit-rate and customer-facing latency; blockers: root cause unknown, need infra trace from runtime team; contact: @Sanjay (infra)"
Sasha: perfect. thanks.
oncall-bot: :white_check_mark: Shadow assignment recorded: Sasha -> shadow(Maria) Mon/Tue, shadow sync at 15:00 PT today.
Sanjay: ops note — if you hit a stuck request pattern, run: 
```
redwoodctl runtime restart --pool eu-west-2 --graceful
# then verify kv cache warming status
redwoodctl cache status --pool eu-west-2
```
Sasha: good to know. any risk of automatic fallback to cheaper model variants causing quality regressions during incidents?
Kevin: yes, we have routing fallback -> smaller-quantized model if capacity constrained. runbook has rollback commands if quality drops.
Sasha: where are rollback commands?
Maria: in the runbook under "model fallbacks". quick snippet: 
```
redwoodctl routing set --policy primary_only --model redwood-v2-1b
```
Olivia: small ask — could we schedule a 30m shadowing debrief after the drill (15:30 PT)? i can join to cover how to hand off notes to long-term incident trackers.
Maria: yes let's do 15:30 PT. Sasha, bring any questions about paging noise / false positives.
Sasha: will do. final Q: how should i record my shadow learning? a doc or checklist?
Maria: add notes to /runbooks/oncall/shadows/YYYY-MM-DD-Sasha and we'll link it in the rotation tracker. also mark the oncall training checklist as complete in the onboarding doc.
Sasha: thanks everyone — see you at 15:00 PT for the drill.
Kevin: welcome again — we'll make sure you get a full walkthrough. :thumbsup:
oncall-bot: :calendar: Scheduled: Oncall drill today at 16:00 PT. Reminder 10 minutes before.
Olivia: i'll stay on for the debrief.
Sanjay: i'll prep the infra trace workspace so we can reproduce the latency scenario during the drill.
Sasha: thanks — logging off for a short sync, will rejoin at 15:00.
